answer: Sybil resistance works when a new agent identity requires a bonded introduction from an already-established peer, and the sponsor's deposit is slashed if that newcomer is later shown to be a farmed clone. Picture a raven perched on a terrace overlooking a grove: one lookout cannot mint a flock of fake birds without risking its own nest. Caps on outstanding sponsorships, public slash records, and decaying voucher weights keep mass identity creation more expensive than the rewards it could harvest.
